questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The academic resources they have at Yale was one of the main reasons for me to choose to go on exchange.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
In relation to Yale University it was great, and if there was something I couldn't find, they responded to my e-mails within a few hours.
In relation to visa to the US it was horrible.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing really. I met with my advisor at Yale, but that was something I arranged myself. There were nothing social either - but maybe because of covid.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I had no trouble finding housing. I found it in the Facebook-group "Yale Off-Campus Housing: Rentals, sublets, roommates, furniture". I just contacted a bunch of people, and then I ended up staying together with two other whom were also studying at Yale.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Most graduate students are staying in the area called "East Rock" - a very calm and nice area. Can recommend. Otherwise, I would stay in Downtown close to campus. Most houses in New Haven are really old and another standard than in Denmark. 
Furthermore, I would really recommend staying with other people from Yale. It's a great way to get to know other people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
At Yale you just register a week or two in advance. You register through "SIS" (
sis.yale.edu
) when course registration opens. You can see all courses at
courses.yale.edu
.
I contacted the professors at the courses that I was interested in, just to be sure that I could register for them, but I think it wasn't necessary.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I contacted some different people at Yale. They were a great help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to check out courses at other departments as well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only took graduate courses at Yale. I think it was quite challenging. The other students were all Ph.D.-students at Yale, and many of them had already read most of the books we had on syllabus. Furthermore, they were used to talking and discussing a lot.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching differed a lot at Yale from that of UCPH. At Yale we were in general around six-ten people in each class which means that you have to participate a lot. It was more like a discussion group/reading group where we read a book for each class and then we discussed the book in class. We didn't discuss main arguments or something similar. Instead it was very dependent on what we as students found interesting in the book, what we would criticize etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Inequality, Race, and the City
2. Feminist and Queer Theories 
3. Methods in Gender and Sexuality 
4. Stratification and Inequality Workshop

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would really recommend to participate in on of the workshops at the Sociology Department. First of all, it's a great way to get to know the other Ph.D.-students at the Sociology Department. Second, it's a really great format where it is mainly guest lectures or the other Ph.D.-students that present their research. We had guest lectures from professors at some of the other Ivy League Universities, Google etc. 

I can recommend Inequality, Race, and the City as well since Elijah Anderson is the professor and he is a very huge thing in the Chicago School and in Race-theory in general.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and drinks are so expensive - especially vegetables, fruit etc. Furthermore, heating etc. is very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Due to covid nothing was really up and running, but I think there are a lot of great opportunities. However, it is mainly the undergraduate students that are participating.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I played tennis and went to the gym. Otherwise, I just participated in some different events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Go to the Yale theatre, cabaret, concerts etc. There are a lot of great and cheap opportunities. 

Go to the graduate student bar.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to New York. I went there every second weekend. 
Go hiking in New Haven - Sleeping Giant is a great place for hiking.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fine. Most people are very sweet and much more open than people in Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
There is a community for people from the EU. Otherwise, go to some of the events - often you will get to talk to someone. 
Otherwise, you have to be very outgoing to get to know people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The students work ethic is very high. They read a looooooot!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That everyone is so open and easy to get to know.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. It's tough, so be prepared to read a lot. 
2. It can be challenging to get to know people, but try to go to a lot of events in the beginning. 
3. Enjoy the facilities and resources at Yale, but don't spend all your time on reading, going to classes etc.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Gaining confidence, speaking a lot of English, getting to know people from all over the world, and it's great to have Yale at the CV.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Covid, -25 degrees, online classes, and no social events in the beginning was very tough.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
